p02.why: A width-3 bit-field promotes to int, a width-40 one keeps long long, and unsigned:32 promotes to unsigned.

p03.why: A pointer to a member function without noexcept does not convert to one with noexcept.

p04.why: 65 and 255 are constants that fit their targets, so neither brace initialization narrows.

p07.why: -1 converts to unsigned before the bitwise operator, so each static_assert holds.

p08.why: An int variable holding zero is not a null pointer constant.

p09.why: Converting const int* to void* would remove const.

p10.why: Steps 4 and 3 give unsigned, unsigned long, and unsigned long long.

p11.why: A zero literal in parentheses is a null pointer constant.

p12.why: Each context converts implicitly outside braces, so 2.7 becomes 2 and the asserts hold.

p13.why: nullptr does not convert to an integer type.

p14.why: The string literal becomes a pointer, and a pointer does not convert to int.

p15.why: With -m32, Clang and GCC give infinity and accept; EDG ILP32 rejects the conversion in constant evaluation (Q-0028).

p16.why: bool, char8_t, char16_t, wchar_t, and unsigned short promote to int, and char32_t to unsigned int.

p17.why: B is an ambiguous base of D.

p19.why: Outside braces, 5 gives true, zeros give false, a non-null pointer gives true, and a null pointer gives false.

p21.why: With -m32 long cannot hold every unsigned value, so step 6 gives unsigned long.

p22.why: A pointer to a member of base B converts to a pointer to member of D.

p27.why: Clang and GCC give infinity at run time, which is above 3e38.

p28.why: 1 is not a null pointer constant and does not convert to a pointer.

p29.why: A pointer to an array of known bound converts to one of unknown bound.

p30.why: 1, 0, and the constant char 1 fit in bool, so the braces do not narrow.

p31.why: The enumerations promote to the first type that holds all their values: int, unsigned int, and long.

p32.why: 16777216 is a constant that float holds exactly.

p33.why: Each integer conversion keeps the low bits: ~0u, 44, and 65534.

p34.why: 0.0/0.0 is a NaN on the IEEE type, and a NaN converts to true.

p35.why: The sequence to Base* forms although Base is a private base, take(Base*) beats the ellipsis, and the chosen conversion is then rejected.

p36.why: A pointer to member does not convert to an integer type.

p37.why: -1.0 to unsigned is undefined, so the constant evaluation fails.

p39.why: A pointer to a noexcept member function converts to one without noexcept.

p40.why: A fixed underlying type converts first and then promotes; char32_t promotes to unsigned int.

p41.why: const is added at every level above the changed level.

p42.why: An array and a function name become pointers, also under unary +.

p43.why: A character literal with value zero is not a null pointer constant (Clang and GCC reject; EDG accepts, Q-0100).

p44.why: Step 3 gives the type of higher rank in each case.

p45.why: nullptr converts to bool only in direct initialization.

p46.why: D* and D& convert to the accessible unique base B.

p55.why: The literal false is not a null pointer constant.
